evidence_establishes: Pull-up shot rates vary across teams and contexts (SF-APPM-058).
Playoff pull-up PPP allowed increases, share decreases (SF-APPS-012).
Within-game adaptation toward counters can produce apparent PPP lifts of +0.05–0.07, but these have been traced to regression to the mean (SF13) and label/mechanical-floor artefacts (SF-APPA-001).
Naïve defensive-channel lifts shrink substantially (often by >50%) when opponent adjustments are considered (SF-APPA-067).
Small-sample per-unit lift analyses (n~15-54) are unreliable and can render a question unanswerable (SF-APPA-066).
Labelling defensive schemes from NBA matchup data is unreliable at high confidence (SF-APPS-058).
evidence_does_not_establish: No study has directly tested whether pull-up shots after PNR failures yield a league-wide lift meeting the 70%/2pp threshold.
The base-rate and playoff findings are descriptive; they do not address causation or counter-factual effects.
The adaptation-artifact studies used different triggers (scheme adaptation, not PNR-fail) and did not evaluate pull-up-only counter strategies.
The shrinkage observed in SF-APPA-067 was for TOV-force channels, not for PNR-fail → pull-up sequences.
own_inferences: Operationalising 'PNR fail' requires a decision about what constitutes a failure (e.g., PNR possession with zero points, turnover, shot-clock violation). The available play-type possession records can identify PNR plays and points, making it feasible to flag failure events.

The counter (pull-up) must be linked temporally; measuring it on the same possession after an offensive rebound could confound the association. A definition like 'first shot attempt after a PNR failure, before the defensive team gains control and new substitutions occur' would reduce contamination.

If the analysis simply compares pull-up PPP after real failures vs all other pull-ups, it will be vulnerable to the same regression-to-the-mean bias that made SF13 an artefact. A valid test must incorporate a placebo/falsification framework.

Pooling multiple seasons can increase per-unit sample sizes, but many team×opponent pairs will still have very few events; the required median lift of 2 pp with ≥70 % positive units is ambitious given typical PPP variability.
uncertainties: The exact unit of analysis (team-offense, team-defense pair, player) is unspecified; testability strongly depends on this choice.
The question does not specify whether 'lift' is relative to a team's own baseline pull-up PPP, to league average, or to some expected value; this affects both computation and power.

The 2025-26 season is only complete through 2026-04-13 (regular season) and 2026-06-21 (playoffs), limiting available full-season data to 2022-23 through 2024-25, plus a partial 2025-26; stationarity across seasons is unknown.
It is unclear how to define a 'unit' for the 70 % criterion—treating each team-offence independently, each team-offence×team-defense pair, or something else—which changes the multiplicity adjustment.

historical_effect.explanation: Prior findings of artefact in similar counter-adaptation studies (SF13, SF-APPA-001) and demonstrations of sample-size problems (SF-APPA-066) changed the assessment from a naive 'proceed' to 'proceed_with_changes', because a simple lift computation would likely reproduce regression-to-the-mean artefacts and fail to provide credible evidence. The design now incorporates placebo comparisons, minimum-exposure gates, and falsification tests.

blocking_constraints.text: Many team-offence × team-defence units will have very few PNR-fail→pull-up sequences, making lift estimates noisy and undermining the 70 % threshold.

Choosing to examine only possessions where the offence followed a failure with a pull-up introduces selection bias; the apparent lift may reflect regression to the mean rather than a true counter effect.

The accuracy of labelling a possession as a PNR failure and of identifying a subsequent pull-up shot depends on the play-type derivation pipeline; misclassification could attenuate or inflate the lift.

prior_work.summary: Prior related work demonstrated that naïve within-game adaptation to suggested counters produces artefactual PPP lifts (SF13, SF-APPA-001), that small-sample per-unit lift decompositions are unreliable (SF-APPA-066), and that labelling defensive schemes is difficult (SF-APPS-058). Pull-up shot rates and base PPP are described (SF-APPM-058, SF-APPS-012). No study has directly tested the PNR-fail → pull-up counter hypothesis with the 70 %/2 pp threshold.

risks.text: Per-unit event counts may be too low to estimate lift with useful precision, especially if units are team × opponent pairs.
Using actual pull-up-after-failure events without a proper control group risks conflating a true counter effect with regression to the mean.
Operational definitions of PNR failure and pull-up shots could introduce classification error that biases the lift estimate.
Testing whether ≥70 % of units show lift >0 requires careful multiplicity control; failure to adjust could create false-positive compliance with the criterion.
Opponent defensive quality, game situation (e.g., late shot-clock pull-ups), and team offensive strength may confound the observed lift.

design.estimand: Average PPP on pull-up shot possessions that immediately follow a PNR failure (same offensive sequence, before opponent change of possession) minus a baseline average pull-up PPP for the same unit, adjusted for pre-failure shooting trends and opponent strength.
design.unit: team-offence × team-defence pair per season (primary); alternative: team-offence only, pooling across opponents.
design.sample: All regular-season games from 2022-23 through 2025-26 (complete to 2026-04-13), excluding garbage time (score margin >20, final 5 minutes).
design.power: Apply a minimum of 20 observed pull-up-after-failure events per unit; pool across seasons to meet threshold. Simulate power to detect a 2 pp lift with 80 % power at alpha=0.05 after multiplicity correction; report units that pass the exposure gate.
design.controls: Adjust for the unit’s average pull-up PPP in non-failure contexts, recent 10-possession rolling shooting percentage, game quarter, and opponent defensive rating. Use a difference-in-differences specification relative to a matched sample of pseudo-failure possessions (PNR successes with similar game-state characteristics).
design.falsification: 1) Placebo test: compute lift after pseudo-failures (PNR successes with similar time/score) and require that the true-failure lift differs significantly from the placebo lift. 2) Specificity test: show that the lift does not generalise to the very next play type that is not a pull-up (e.g., post-failure DRIVE). 3) Out-of-time validation: estimate the 70 %/2 pp rule on 2022-23 to 2024-25, then hold out 2025-26 and check stability of the classification.
design.multiplicity: Apply Benjamini-Hochberg correction to the per-unit lift-to-zero tests. Report the proportion of units with significant lift >0 (with 95 % CI) and the bootstrapped 95 % confidence interval of the median lift.
design.decision_rule: Consider the counter 'real' if: (a) at least 70 % of eligible units have lift >0 after multiplicity correction, (b) the lower bound of the bootstrapped median lift CI exceeds 2 pp, (c) the true-failure lift is significantly larger than the placebo lift, and (d) the out-of-time validation does not reverse the conclusion.
design.data_version: 2022-23 through 2024-25 regular seasons (full) plus 2025-26 regular season (complete as of 2026-04-13); playoffs excluded from primary analysis to avoid small-sample/variance artefacts.
